transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Anna Park (CTO - Hearthwell), Raj Patel (Infra Eng), Liza Gomez (Security Lead)
Shared links: playbook draft: https://redwood.ai/pilot/1234-playbook, telemetry sheet: https://redwood.ai/pilot/1234-telemetry, pricing addendum (placeholder)

Summary section (auto): We went through observed errors in the last 48h window; two spikes where vpc-egress threw TCP resets toward our private nodes, and one instance where model fallback didn't trigger because of mismatched model variant tags. Also discussed missing telemetry around KV-cache eviction counters and batching latencies.

00:00 Maya: All right folks, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this to an hour. Uh, quick roundtable - Diego from our SE team will lead the telemetry bit, and then we'll go into the routing incidents and the kernel upgrade plan.
00:22 Anna: Thanks, Maya. I just want to say last week's run flagged a couple of pretty bad p95 spikes for us so appreciate the follow-up.
00:30 Diego: Yep, saw that. I pulled the traces — Raj if I remember right you uploaded the egress tcpdump and the traceroutes?
00:39 Raj: Yeah, uploaded last night, the file name is traceroute-egress-1129.pcap. I also gave you the kube-proxy logs, there was a flurry of conntrack entries.
00:48 Diego: Cool. So first order we found two patterns: one, there are intermittent blackholes between AZ-b and AZ-c that show as retransmits then RSTs; two, when the request latency hit the top of the bucket, our routing policy didn't match the tag for the fallback model variant. Somewhere the model-version header got normalized to a short tag and the router's rule didn't match.
01:10 Raj: On the blackholes, we think it's an MTU path issue maybe compounded by an intermediate firewall doing MSS clamping incorrectly. I couldn't find consistent packet drops but saw fragmentation and RSTs.
01:22 Liza: From security's perspective, we want to be sure any changes to egress rules or kernel tunables are reviewed. We also need the KMS/HSM flow documented — how keys are requested for encrypted caches.
01:35 Diego: Understood. On telemetry, the big ask from you all was better visibility into the KV cache (the K V cash, speech-to-text in our export sometimes shows it weird) — eviction_count, hit_rate per-prefix, and batching queue length per worker. Right now you only have aggregated token count and latency histogram.
01:52 Anna: Exactly, the aggregated metrics mask the hot prefixes that cause bursty latency. Also, the prefix cache warmed in one test but then got evicted under the load, which caused a cascade of long tail.
02:03 Maya: So proposed immediate items: Diego will add the telemetry fields and a mapping doc; Raj will run a targeted 30 minute pinned-model load that reproduces the high-concurrency path; and we will schedule a kernel upgrade during a maintenance window with a clear rollback.
02:18 Raj: Quick question on the kernel upgrade — which kernel? You're proposing the custom inference kernel 1.12 that includes the attention optimization and quantization-friendly path?
02:27 Diego: Yeah, 1.12 build. It has the optimized grouping for attention and fixes a known memory leak in the kv-lru. Our internal tests show p50 and p95 improvement but there is a risk of new NIC driver interactions.
02:40 Raj: Right, our infra uses a slightly customized Mellanox driver stack, so that concerns me.
02:46 Diego: That's why the playbook includes rollback: we snapshot the instance (or checkpoint using our container snapshot flow), stage kernel on one canary, run our smokebench (10k tokens across 3 model widths), and if any packet-level retransmit > 0.5% then rollback.
03:05 Anna: I want the rollback criteria explicit and the owner for each step. Also we need the SRE on-call notified automatically by webhook.
03:14 Maya: Agreed. Action item: Diego writes step-by-step playbook and I'll collect owners — add it to the shared doc by Friday.
03:22 Diego: Also on fallback routing — we've seen policy mismatches when model variants are auto-aliased by your CI. Solution: tag models with immutable version refs and use model-id in routing policies rather than semantic tags. We'll add a routing policy that checks compatibility and falls back to the nearest-compatible variant (smaller quant, CPU-friendly) rather than failing.
03:42 Raj: That sounds good but two asks: one, can fallback be region-aware so it doesn't route across continents for latency sensitive calls; and two, can we have a circuit-breaker so the fallback only engages after N failures within the last M seconds?
03:55 Diego: Yes to both — policy supports region affinity and a sliding window circuit-breaker. We'll show config examples in the playbook: e.g., fallback.threshold = 5 failures / 30s and fallback.region_policy = local_then_adjacent.
04:14 Liza: On the security front, aside from the KMS questions, we need to ensure audit logs are preserved for 1 year and that token-level observability doesn't leak PII into logs.
04:25 Maya: We already have token redaction at the application layer — we'll show the config. Diego, can you attach the audit retention config?
04:32 Diego: Yes, add a section 'audit_retention' in the playbook, default 365 days, and S3 lifecycle rule example.
04:41 Anna: Back to telemetry — when will the new metrics show up in our Grafana?
04:45 Diego: If you add the new scrape job and we push the mapping you'll see them within the next 24 hours; the playbook includes the prometheus labels.
04:54 Raj: I'll add the scrape config today. Also I'll send the traceroute and tcpdump links to Diego for deeper analysis.
05:02 Diego: Thanks. On the egress MSS/MTU suspicion — please check for any firewall translation devices that do MSS clamping; sometimes the cloud provider middleboxes do that. If you can get a path MTU discovery trace that'd help.
05:15 Raj: Will do.
05:18 Maya: Competitor note— Anna asked earlier if we compared our routing fallback to what FastEndpoint offers; quick summary, FastEndpoint does aggressive global reroute but less observability and fewer rollback safeguards; CloudServeAI has a one-click model fallback but it's opaque. We're pitching controlled, observable fallbacks.
05:36 Anna: That matches what we want, observable is key.
05:40 Diego: One more technical note: KV cache eviction counters are emitted at worker granularity in our runtime but not at prefix level by default; we'll add a -prefix-dim flag so you can see which prefix caused the eviction. It's lightweight but not enabled by default.
05:56 Raj: If there's a perf cost we need to know how much CPU overhead that prefix-dim adds.
06:03 Diego: We'll include cost estimates in the telemetry doc — expect ~2-3% CPU uptick under heavy load.
06:12 Liza: And confirm the telemetry pipeline strips any user-provided messages that match PII regex patterns before storing.
06:20 Diego: Yes we'll show the redaction regex and the hook point in the exporter.
06:26 Maya: OK recapping next steps — Diego upload playbook and telemetry mapping; Raj run pinned-model load and share flamegraphs; Maya send pricing addendum; Liza finalize SOC2 questions. We'll reconvene same time next week unless something urgent comes up.
06:45 Anna: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:50 Maya: Thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: Diego will attach a sample fallback policy snippet: 
- fallback: { threshold: 5, window: 30s, region_policy: "local_then_adjacent", preferred_variants: ["model-v1-quant", "model-v1-cpu"] }
Diego will also include a smokebench script and the exact rollback conditions. Raj to provide the PCAPs and the MTU probe output. Liza will enumerate required SOC2 controls (logging, key management, access reviews). Maya to follow up on pricing and send a calendar invite for the kernel upgrade dry-run.

Transcript end.
